title: Grid Edge Engagement — deployment proposal and experiment journal
content:
Purpose and context:
Summary: notes + short proposal for a utility customer POC (grid-edge telemetry ingestion + incident summarization). Goal is a low-cost, low-latency assistant that extracts anomalies, summarizes event chains, and generates human-readable incident narratives for field technicians. Customer constraints: air-gapped regional site, intermittent connectivity, strict PII removal on-device, 200ms median generation target for single-turn diagnostic queries, 95th percentile < 750ms for short summaries (~80–150 tokens). Budget: target token-equivalent cost <= 0.03 USD per summary on Dedicated capacity.

Key objectives for POC:
- Validate model variants for 1) short diagnostic Q&A and 2) multi-document event summarization.
- Measure latency and token-cost tradeoffs for per-region dedicated pools and private deployment options.
- Establish prompt/pipeline patterns that are robust to chunked telemetry and structured sensor attachments.
- Produce an integration checklist for the customer's OT team and a minimal rollback plan.

Datasets and evaluation:
- Sources: anonymized telemetry traces (5M rows), 400 labelled incident summaries (human-curated), operator Q&A logs (1.2k), config snapshots.
- Eval sets: small-QA (800 cases), summary set (200 cases), adversarial prompts (missing fields, scrambled timestamps) (150 cases).
- Metrics: ROUGE-L / BERTScore for summaries, top-1 accuracy for attribute extraction, mean latency (cold and warm), memory/VRAM footprint, failure modes (hallucination rate on entity extraction).

Model variants to test (initial matrix):
- Variant A (accuracy-first): 13B dense checkpoint (fp16) served on Dedicated A100; baseline latency expected higher, quality highest.
- Variant B (quantized short): 13B Q4_0 (PTQ) using optimized kernels + KV cache retention; target for short QA.
- Variant C (tiny cascade): 3B quantized small model for candidate extraction, with 13B for rerank/summarize (cascade).
- Variant D (edge-optimized): 7B int8 dynamic quant + structured pruning for on-prem device (if customer requests air-gapped on-prem).

Quantization approaches and rationale:
- PTQ (post-training quantization) Q4_0 for latency wins on short-turn Q&A; minimal engineering overhead. Expect slight drop on abstractive summarization — needs eval gating.
- QAT (quantization-aware) options flagged for later if PTQ fails to meet accuracy guardrails on entity extraction. Reserve for >2-week iteration only.
- Mixed-precision fallback: keep fp16 reserved for first 32 tokens in generation for safety-critical prompts, then switch to quantized execution for subsequent tokens (reduce early-token hallucination).

Prompt and pipeline patterns (proposed):
1) Ingest: small rolling window + schema extractor (rule-based) to normalize timeseries into canonical records.
2) Retriever: lightweight embedding index on-device (sparse) for recent events, TTL 24h. Query/recall limited to top-6 chunks.
3) Candidate extraction: short model (3B quant) returns structured attributes (timestamp, device id, metric, anomaly flag). Use template-based prompts for high precision; include explicit don't-invent policy.
4) Rerank + summarize: larger model (13B quant or dense) constructs human summary. Prompt includes: explicit context lines (max 6), bullet constraints, expected length, forbidden PII markers, and 'if unsure say ambiguous'.
5) Safety and redaction: post-process pipeline removes sensitive fields using deterministic regex + ML extractor ensemble.

Batching, caching, and routing notes:
- Continuous batching: enable micro-batching window of 10ms for Dedicated pools in region; watch tail latency.
- KV caching: cache recent device histories per-session (TTL 120s). For summarization flows, pre-warm KV cache with the last 1–2KB of context.
- Smart routing: route low-latency QA to quantized variants; route high-quality summaries to fp16 reserved pool with cost accounting. Implement automatic fallback if latency SLOs fail.

Experiment matrix and acceptance criteria:
- Short-QA (800 cases): Variant B median <= 180ms, 90th <= 420ms, extraction precision >= 94%. If pass -> promote to canary for real traffic.
- Summary (200 cases): Variant A (dense) baseline; Variant B must achieve >= 0.88 relative BERTScore to baseline and median latency <= 600ms.
- Cascade evaluation: end-to-end latency for cascade <= 700ms with accuracy parity within 4% of dense baseline.

Workshop agenda (on-site, day-long):
- AM: customer goals & constraints, data handoff, security checklist (30m).
- Mid-morning: quick baseline runs (small-QA) on local infra + observe latency (90m).
- Lunch: design session — prompt templates + redaction policy (60m).
- PM: run quant experiments (PTQ) + failure-mode triage (120m).
- Close: prioritization and next steps (30m).

Operational checklist for private deployment:
- KMS/HSM integration notes: require offline key provisioning; test with sample encryption key.
- Network: allow specific port ranges for update sync; ensure no egress for sensory payloads.
- Logging: structured audit logs only to local syslog; scrub fields before periodic sync.
- Rollback: maintain previous model artifact and routing policy pinned for 24h after rollout.

Open questions / risks (items to resolve in follow-ups):
- Can the customer accept a 4–6% accuracy drop for the cost/latency improvements? Decision owner: Customer PM.
- Data labelling: 200 summaries may be insufficient for robust abstractive eval; need to budget additional label effort (estimate 1.5 engineer-weeks or outsource 150 summaries).
- Air-gapped inference image signing: how will the customer manage updates? Contact security lead.

Immediate action items (owner + ETA):
- Prepare PTQ recipe for 13B checkpoint and run locally (Ethan Park) — ETA 2025-11-18.
- Generate short-QA eval harness and seed 800-case set (Sofia Patel) — ETA 2025-11-15.
- Draft customer-facing two-pager (Marisol Chen) summarizing tradeoffs and SLOs — ETA 2025-11-20.

Notes to self / shorthand observations:
- Avoid overfitting prompts to curated summaries; keep a 'no-new-facts' guard.
- If PTQ shows entity hallucination, add a verification pass using the 3B extractor as hard filter.
- Consider a future UX: inline suggested fixes for ambiguous timestamps.
